questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with a vastly different study and living culture compared to Denmark, further I also wanted to go to a university that was academically challenging.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing as you are sent a lot of mails and it can be hard to find out which are actually important.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None except written instructions and guides.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was a series of different housing types which you could apply for in 3 different rounds, they had different styles of living as well as different cultures.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my type of housing there was a meal plan included.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It makes the studying much more immersive and an overall better experience in my opinion.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is 3 rounds of applications together with an appeal period. In each round you list what courses you would like to get, after which you will be given some or all of them, for the appeal you can try to change to different courses if there is one or more you are unhappy with.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a website called NUSMods that lists all the courses, descriptions, reviews as well as prerequisites. Note that not all the courses on the website will be available to you as an exchange student and you will be sent lists with the courses you can actually take.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a long lists of courses that you would like, I personally applied for around 10-12 in total. Further do not stress if you do not get all your courses right away or have issues and the administration is very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took bachelor courses ranging from 2k - 4k with most of them being 3k courses meaning they are meant for people on their 3rd year of their bachelor. Overall, I think they were around the high-end in terms of difficulty compared to the courses I have had at UCPH however, not much more difficuly.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were very similar to those at UCPH however, the tutorials / exercises classes were very different. Rather than solving the questions in class with a TA you would solve them at home and then just have the TA or professor go over the answer either giving it to you directly or making different students present their answer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Non-Linear Programming (MA3236), Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (CS3243), Computer Graphics (CS3241), Optimisation Algorithms (CS4234), Greek Philosophy (PH2222)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really likes CS3243 as it had a very good blend of theory and practical use, further CS4234 and MA3236 were also very interesting  and challenging courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a club for basically anything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything they are interested in, it is a great way to make local friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel, there is definitely things to see and do in SG: lots of amazing hawker centers, large malls, bar strips and other tourist like activities. However, you quickly run out and with SG located where it is it is super cheap to travel to all the other countries in south-east Asia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It takes a little bit as the people are very traditional.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students can be a bit shy and weary of exchange students so it is very hard to get to know them unless in participate in clubs or other activities with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They have very different attitudes to going out and the way in which they hang out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They can be quite straight forward.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to get your sing pass and permanent Singapore number early, having Revolut makes it a lot easier to split bills with other exchange students, some locals have it as well. Try to keep organized and get all the administrative matters done early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling with other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the way they study.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
